subject: Dedicated reservation: phased wedge reserve & warmup schedule
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mariner.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mariner.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity options — wedge reserve & warmup hypothesis

Samir / Alyssa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I put together a compact set of reservation options designed to match Mariner's bursty training/eval profile while keeping predictable unit economics. The attached PDF is the short proposal; the workbook contains the traffic assumptions I used. High level: 

- Wedge reserve concept: three activation tiers (Pilot, Scale, Peak) allowing you to ramp without committing full capacity up front.
- Min guaranteed GPUs (Pilot floor) keeps latency SLOs intact while we warm caches and KV layers.
- Warmup credits and pre-warm windows to minimize cold-start token penalties on heavy batched jobs.

Numbers (example):
- Pilot floor: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (min guarantee)
- Scale tranche: +24 GPUs (36 total) at month 3 trigger
- Peak tranche: +12 GPUs (48 total) at month 6 or on 75% sustained utilization

Can you confirm the 12 GPU pilot floor looks reasonable against your early production traffic? If you prefer, we can swap to a 16 GPU pilot to reduce queueing for short-lived high-concurrency requests.

Next steps: if the structure looks good I'll pull together a redlineable PDF and a short canary run plan for week-of activation.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Redwood_Wedge_Reserve_Proposal_v4.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
Attachment: Mariner_Workbook_capacity_playbook.xlsx (XLSX, 220KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mariner.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mariner.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — wedge reserve & warmup hypothesis

Camila —

Appreciate the crisp framing. The wedge approach aligns with our internal risk tolerance and budget windows. A few clarifying Qs: 

1) On the 12 GPU pilot floor — what is the expected average QPS and percentiles you modeled for the 95th p99 latency? We need to ensure we don't underprovision for small, latency-sensitive inference calls.
2) How do warmup credits apply if we run a daily batch job at 02:00 UTC that spikes KV misses for an hour?
3) Any constraints on region affinity? We want the pilot in us-west-2 and prefer not to cross-region failover unless absolutely required.

Also copying Alyssa for capacity-planning input. If these look acceptable we can schedule a 30-min call next week to align legal and infra.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure | Mariner AI
samir.patel@mariner.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@mariner.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mariner.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — wedge reserve & warmup hypothesis

Samir / Alyssa —

Great questions. Quick answers and then a suggested canary cadence: 

1) Pilot floor modeling: 12 A100-eq was sized for an expected 250 QPS steady-state of short-text inference (median token length ~40) with p95 latency goal <120ms and p99 <350ms under continuous traffic. The workbook uses your provided 40% cache-hit baseline; if you expect lower cache hit we recommend shifting to a 16 GPU pilot.

2) Warmup credits: we offer a rolling warmup credit that covers the first 90 minutes of high cold-KV churn per 24h window for the pilot. For your 02:00 UTC daily batch we can schedule a pre-warm window (30–60 minutes) to be excluded from burn-rate calculations — documented in the SLA addendum. Excess beyond credits is billed at the standard per-token rate.

3) Region affinity: we can pin the pilot to us-west-2. Cross-region failover will remain an optional fallback and will only be used under capacity exhaustion; data plane stays in us-west-2.

Suggested canary:
- Week 0–2 (Pilot): 12 GPUs, warmup windows mornings PST (02:00 UTC pre-warm), limited to 20% of traffic for safety.
- Week 3–8 (Scale): expand to 36 GPUs if sustained 60% utilization for 7 days; increase traffic share to 60%.
- Week 9–24 (Peak unlock): move to 48 GPUs once policy triggers or at next pricing tranche.

I've looped in Karthik to confirm the activation playbook and Marissa for pricing approval on the warmup credit terms. I've also attached a lighter one-page timeline for exec review.

Camila
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Wedge_Activation_Timeline_onepager.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — wedge reserve & warmup hypothesis

Samir / team —

Quick note from the ops side: we can commit the us-west-2 pilot floor at 12 A100-equivalent GPUs starting Dec 7 (week-of activation) with a 48–72hr pre-warm staging window. The activation runbook will include: 

- Canary route: 10% traffic initially isolated to a dedicated lane, with telemetry for token latency, KV hit-rate, and GPU utilization.
- Autoscale gates: scale-to-36 only after 7 consecutive days >60% avg utilization; manual override available.
- Fallback policy: if p99 latency >500ms for 6 consecutive hours we automatically divert 30% traffic to the hosted fallback model (with prior approval) while debugging.

Marissa, pricing/credit sign-off? Camila, I added the exact playbook to the workbook tab "Activation_Runbook". Samir, if you confirm the Dec 7 start we will get legal a short SOW and bring the proposal to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
